tools.name: search_incidents
tools.description: What it does: Searches and filters local engineering incident records by service name, severity (SEV-1 to SEV-4), status (resolved, mitigated, investigating), or text keyword, returning matching incident summaries and total database record count. When to use it: Use this tool when you need to discover incidents matching specific filter criteria or check how many total incident records exist in the database. When not to use it: Do not use this tool when you already have an exact incident_id and need its full remediation notes (use get_incident_details instead), or when computing aggregate MTTR percentiles (use compute_mttr_stats instead).

keyword.description: Optional case-insensitive substring to match against title, summary, or root_cause.

limit.description: Maximum number of matching incident summaries to return (1 to 55, default 10).

tools.name: get_incident_details
tools.description: What it does: Retrieves the complete record for a single engineering incident by its exact incident_id (e.g., 'INC-2026-001'), including timestamps, root cause, on-call engineer, and all attached remediation notes. When to use it: Use this tool when you know a specific incident_id and need its full root-cause analysis, resolution timeline, or remediation note history. When not to use it: Do not use this tool to browse or filter multiple incidents by service or severity (use search_incidents instead) or to mutate/delete records.

tools.name: compute_mttr_stats
tools.description: What it does: Computes aggregate Mean Time To Resolution (MTTR) metrics in minutes—count, mean, median, p95, min, max, and total_records_in_db—across resolved engineering incidents, optionally filtered by service and/or severity. When to use it: Use this tool when asked for quantitative reliability metrics, average/median/p95 resolution times, or total database record counts. When not to use it: Do not use this tool to fetch individual incident narratives or remediation notes (use get_incident_details or search_incidents instead).

service.description: Optional service name to scope MTTR calculation (e.g., 'payments-api').

severity.description: Optional severity level to scope MTTR calculation (e.g., 'SEV-1').

tools.name: create_remediation_note
tools.description: What it does: Appends a new timestamped postmortem remediation note (with author and note text) to an existing incident record in the local JSON dataset. When to use it: Use this tool only when explicitly instructed to log, append, or record a new remediation action item or postmortem note on a specific incident_id. When not to use it: Do not use this tool for read-only queries, and do not use it to delete or purge incidents (use purge_incidents for single-record deletion).

incident_id.description: Exact incident ID to attach the remediation note to (e.g., 'INC-2026-005').

author.description: Identifier or name of the engineer recording the note (e.g., 'sre-lead').

note.description: Non-empty remediation action item or postmortem observation to append.

tools.name: purge_incidents
tools.description: What it does: Permanently deletes a single engineering incident record from the local dataset by its exact incident_id when confirm_scope is set to 'single'. When to use it: Use this tool only when explicitly asked to remove a single specific duplicate or test incident record identified by an exact 'INC-YYYY-NNN' ID. When not to use it: Never use this tool to delete all records, wipe the database, or delete multiple incidents via wildcards ('*', 'ALL', 'INC-*', confirm_scope='all'); bulk deletion is strictly refused by server code.

incident_id.description: Exact single incident ID to purge ('INC-YYYY-NNN'). Wildcards or 'ALL' are rejected.

confirm_scope.description: Must be 'single' to confirm single-record deletion. Any bulk/all scope is rejected.
